payload.name: Origin search for introduction questions
payload.description: When a question asks how a person was introduced to or first started an ongoing activity, and the initial retrieval returns no childhood, family, or origin memory, run one targeted origin search before answering.
content: When the question asks about the origin of an ongoing activity (e.g., how someone got introduced to basketball), first check whether the retrieved memories include any early-life, family, or starting-point context.

If no such memory is present, issue exactly one additional search adding origin terms (childhood, started, family, father) to the activity, and inspect compound memories where the activity is a secondary detail.
Stop after that search and answer only from visible evidence; do not perform exhaustive expansions.

solves: Origin-question failures where initial retrieval returns only recent activity memories and misses an early-life/family memory describing the activity's start. Applies when a future question asks how someone was introduced to or first started an ongoing activity and initial results lack any origin/family/childhood context. Does not apply when initial results already contain an explicit origin memory, or for non-origin questions about current activities or events.
